9.text: In the cosmogonical statements of the Chukchee shamans (so-called

10.text: eñeˊñɪlɪnä loˊᵋo, “things seen by a shaman”), we find that the life which they

11.text: believe to be diffused throughout nature is described in its relation to the

12.text: shamanistic spirits in the following manner: —

13.text: “On the steep bank of a river there exists life. A voice is there, and speaks aloud. I saw

14.text: the ‘master’ of the voice and spoke with him. He subjected himself to me and sacrificed to me.

15.text: He came yesterday and answered my questions. The small gray bird with the blue breast sings

16.text: shaman-songs in the hollow of the bough, calls her spirits, and practises shamanism. The wood-

17.text: pecker strikes his drum in the tree with his drumming nose. Under the axe the tree trembles and

18.text: wails as a drum under the bâton. All these come at my call.

19.text: “All that exists lives. The lamp walks around. The walls of the house have voices of their

20.text: own. Even the chamber-vessel has a separate land and house. The skins sleeping in the bags talk

21.text: at night. The antlers lying on the tombs arise at night and walk in procession around the mounds,

22.text: while the deceased get up and visit the living.”¹

38.text: the body of a captive boy who pretends to be dead. The evil spirit defecates

39.text: into the vessel, and bids it keep watch over the body. After a while the

40.text: boy moves, and the chamber-vessel immediately gives alarm by its cries.

41.text: The spirit, who was asleep, awakes and comes to inspect the prisoner; but
